subject: Task 26.3 - Guard enforcement (scripts/check-agents.sh B1 reports-array attempt listing from phase 20, B2 phase aggregate consistency from phase 26, B3 AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE self-check), audited as a test-quality exercise: do the recorded sensitivity probes genuinely establish that the guards discriminate and are honest?
audit_method: Independent reproduction. No code, script, test, or documentation was modified. All mutations were performed on a throwaway copy at /tmp/final-review/test-quality/repo (docs/, scripts/, .opencode/, AGENTS.md, GOALS.md copied from the working tree). The real tree's `git status --short` and `git diff --numstat` were identical at the start and at the end of this audit, and no phase-26 record exists in the real tree (the fabricated one existed only in the /tmp copy). Mutated inputs (docs/plan/state.json, docs/agent-contracts.md, scripts/check-agents.sh, docs/implementation/20.1/*, docs/implementation/26.2/orchestration.json) were restored and verified byte-identical with `cmp` before each baseline re-run.

findings.description: B1 replaced an ungated, all-phases state-listing check with one gated at `p >= APPLIES_FROM_PHASE` (20), so the contract's '**all phases**' rule that a task with a worker report lists its reviewer-report.json in state.json is no longer enforced below phase 20. The pre-change script failed a phase-15 task whose reviewer-report.json was de-listed; the new script passes it. The narrowing is a side effect of the replacement, not something the 26.3 delegation asked for, and it is disclosed in neither the worker report's `known_limitations` nor `documentation_reconciliation` (which instead asserts the pairing check is 'unchanged' - true of the separate file-existence section, but silent on this scope narrowing). docs/plan/README.md was honestly updated to say 'enforces this from phase 20', but docs/agent-contracts.md's Enforcement scope still says 'all phases' for this rule, so the contract now overstates what the script enforces and the B3 self-check does not cover this rule.
evidence: docs/agent-contracts.md Enforcement scope: '**all phases** - a task that has a `worker-report.json`, and is not listed in `docs/implementation/review-exemptions.json`, lists its `reviewer-report.json` in `docs/plan/state.json` `reports`.'

git diff scripts/check-agents.sh: the removed check `if ! jq -e --arg id "$b" 'any(.phases[].tasks[]; .id == $id and ((.reports // []) | any(test("reviewer-report"))))' "$state"` had no phase gate; the replacement adds `p=${b%%.*}; ... [ "$p" -ge "$APPLIES_FROM_PHASE" ] || continue`.

Reproduced on /tmp copy: removed `docs/implementation/15.1/reviewer-report.json` from task 15.1's reports in docs/plan/state.json -> NEW script: 'check-agents: PASS' (exit 0); HEAD script (`git show HEAD:scripts/check-agents.sh`): 'FAIL: task 15.1 has a reviewer report on disk but docs/plan/state.json does not list it in reports', 'check-agents: FAIL' (exit 1). state.json restored byte-identical (cmp).

Blast radius measured on the real tree: 0 tasks at phase < 20 currently have an unlisted reviewer-report.json on disk (swept all of docs/implementation/*/), so no shipped artifact is currently mis-passing.
docs/agent-contracts.md line 209 ('`scripts/check-agents.sh` enforces the pairing for every other task') refers to the file-existence pairing section, which is unchanged.
findings.recommended_action: Either retain the all-phases reviewer-report listing check as a separate loop (so the 'all phases' contract bullet stays true), or amend the contract bullet to 'from phase 20' to match enforcement and record the narrowing in the worker report's known_limitations. The current mismatch between the contract's 'all phases' wording and phase-20-gated enforcement should not be left implicit.

findings.description: The guard's `role_mix` is computed over task-record invocations only, while `subagent_invocations_total` and the phase_reviewer_* / unsuffixed triples add the phase record's own phase-reviewer entries. The only in-repo record with phase-reviewer entries, phase 20, uses the opposite role_mix convention (it includes `phase-reviewer: 2`). Direction of risk assessed as asked: (a) a WRONG role_mix cannot pass - a role_mix inflated in a phase-26+ record is flagged exactly; (b) a RIGHT-by-precedent record CAN fail - phase 20 is internally consistent on every other field (subagent_invocations_total 13 = 11 + 2, phase_reviewer_invocations 2, phase_reviewer_total_tokens 7814171, total_tokens 90126724 all reconcile) yet fails on role_mix alone. The probes only demonstrate this in the out-of-scope direction (lowering the constant to 20); no probe feeds a phase-20-convention record through the guard in scope, which is the direction that will actually bite when the phase-26 record is written. The risk is a blocking false failure at the phase gate rather than silent false confidence, and the guard's comment block does state the chosen basis, so this is a friction/consistency defect, not a soundness one. It is, to the worker's credit, disclosed in `interpretations`.
evidence: scripts/check-agents.sh: 'role_mix maps each role to its count over all task-record invocations' vs 'subagent_invocations_total = task_level_invocations + phase_reviewer_invocations'.

docs/implementation/phase-20/orchestration.json: subagents length 13, aggregate.task_level_invocations 11, subagent_invocations_total 13, phase_reviewer_invocations 2, role_mix {implementation-worker:4, implementation-reviewer:4, test-quality-reviewer:3, phase-reviewer:2}, phase_reviewer_total_tokens 7814171, task_level_total_tokens 82312553, total_tokens 90126724. Task records 20.1/20.2/20.3 contain no phase-reviewer entries.

Reproduced: AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 -> exactly one mismatch, 'FAIL: phase 20 aggregate does not reconcile with the task records: role_mix: recorded {"implementation-worker":4,"implementation-reviewer":4,"test-quality-reviewer":3,"phase-reviewer":2} != recomputed {"implementation-worker":4,"implementation-reviewer":4,"test-quality-reviewer":3}'. Every other phase-20 field reconciles.

Wrong-record direction is covered: an in-scope record with role_mix {implementation-worker:99, implementation-reviewer:2} -> 'FAIL: ... role_mix: recorded {...} != recomputed {"implementation-worker":2,"implementation-reviewer":2}'.
docs/agent-contracts.md defines no field-level basis for role_mix; it says only 'an `aggregate` whose numeric fields equal the sums recomputed from the task-level records'.
findings.recommended_action: State the role_mix basis (and the phase-reviewer basis for subagent_invocations_total) in docs/agent-contracts.md's phase-aggregate bullet, so a record author cannot reasonably adopt the phase-20 convention. Optionally add a probe that feeds a phase-20-convention record through the guard in scope to record the expected rejection.

findings.description: Part of B2's recomputation is self-referential: `subagent_invocations_total`, `phase_reviewer_invocations`, the three `phase_reviewer_*` sums, and the unsuffixed `cost_usd`/`total_tokens`/`duration_seconds` are derived from the phase record's OWN `subagents` array, not from the task-level records. The contract says the aggregate's numeric fields equal sums 'recomputed from the task-level records', which overstates what is checked for those five fields. The guard does catch internal inconsistency within that portion, but it cannot detect a phase-reviewer invocation that is absent from `subagents` altogether (no other check cross-references the existence of a phase-review record against the phase aggregate). This residual gap is not in the worker report's known_limitations, though the guard comment does acknowledge the 0 case ('0 when the release review was the gate and no separate phase-reviewer record exists').
evidence: Reproduced R2: phase-reviewer entry present in `subagents` but omitted from subagent_invocations_total -> 'FAIL: phase 26 aggregate does not reconcile with the task records: subagent_invocations_total: recorded 4 != recomputed 5'. Self-consistency within the phase-reviewer portion IS enforced.
Reproduced R3: phase-reviewer invocation omitted from `subagents` entirely, aggregate recording phase_reviewer_invocations 0 -> 'check-agents: PASS'. Undetectable by design.
Reproduced R1: phase-reviewer entry added and fully self-consistent -> PASS, confirming the guard accepts arbitrary but internally consistent phase-reviewer accounting.
docs/agent-contracts.md:152-153 'an `aggregate` whose numeric fields equal the sums recomputed from the task-level records'.
findings.recommended_action: Soften the contract wording for the phase-reviewer-derived fields, or add a note that a missing phase-review invocation is out of the guard's reach (the phase review and gate checks are expected to cover it).

findings.description: Tolerance honesty verified by boundary measurement rather than by the single recorded probe. The cost tolerance is absolute 1e-6 and its boundary was mapped: 5.2e-8 PASS, 9.9e-7 PASS, 1.0e-6 FAIL, 1.1e-6 FAIL, 1e-5 FAIL, 0.01 FAIL. The +5.2e-8 boundary probe is reported honestly (it passes, and the report says so and explains why). Token and duration comparisons are exact: +1 token and +1 duration both FAIL. 1e-6 USD is a defensible choice given the recorded phase-17 P17-F1 float-sum scale of 5.2e-8 and double-precision summation noise of order 1e-13, and it still catches every realistic mis-add. The report's known_limitations is actually MORE conservative than reality: it states a dropped/added invocation slips only 'if its cost and all three numeric fields are zero', but I showed an all-zero phantom invocation is still caught by the exact integer count fields. Also verified the tolerance is applied per-field to all three cost fields and does not weaken the integer fields (task_level_cost_usd +5.2e-8 PASSes, as designed).
evidence: Boundary sweep on the independent conforming record (cost delta -> aggregate FAIL count): 5.2e-8 -> 0, 9.9e-7 -> 0, 1.0e-6 -> 1, 1.1e-6 -> 1, 1e-5 -> 1, 0.01 -> 1.
'FAIL: ... cost_usd: recorded 0.126799336 != recomputed 0.116799336 (tolerance 0.000001)' for +0.01.
'FAIL: ... task_level_total_tokens: recorded 9009682 != recomputed 9009681' (+1 token); 'FAIL: ... duration_seconds: recorded 2040 != recomputed 2039' (+1 duration).
D1 (a real invocation dropped from 26.2, aggregate left stale) -> 8 mismatches including exact token and duration differences.

D2 (an all-zero phantom invocation added to 26.2, aggregate left stale) -> still caught: 'task_level_invocations: recorded 4 != recomputed 5; subagent_invocations_total: recorded 4 != recomputed 5; review_rounds: recorded 2 != recomputed 3; task_level_invocations_per_task: ...; role_mix: ...'.
phase_reviewer_cost_usd recorded as 0.001 with zero phase-reviewer entries -> FAIL (the tolerance does not mask a wrong phase-reviewer figure).

summary: The recorded sensitivity probes are genuine and they hold up under independent reproduction. I rebuilt a clean copy at /tmp/final-review/test-quality/repo and reproduced all nine recorded probes with byte-identical failure messages, then added eleven probes the worker did not run. B1 discriminates properly and, importantly, is satisfiable rather than merely fail-on-anything: a correctly listed attempt file PASSes, an attempt with the wrong number FAILS, both the canonical `.attempt-<n>` and legacy `-attempt-<n>` forms are caught, and all six report kinds are exercised. B2 is genuinely discriminating across task_count, per-task invocations, role_mix, review/test/rework counts, tokens, durations and cost; two drift probes the worker did not run show that both a dropped real invocation and even an all-zero phantom invocation are caught by the exact integer fields, which means the report's stated cost-tolerance caveat is more conservative than reality. B3 reproduces exactly, and I confirmed independently that the pre-existing APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20 self-check is still alive and that the two self-checks do not shadow each other. On honesty: the real tree is unmodified (identical git status and diff numstat at start and end of the audit), every mutation I made was confined to the /tmp copy and restored with `cmp`, the real tree's current two-line failure is exactly the transient state the report predicted, and the report does state plainly that phase-26 B2 coverage is currently fabricated-only. The residual gap is narrow and honest: with no real phase-26 record, that branch is unexercised on the shipped tree - but the 26.1-amended phase-21 record reconciles exactly on every field, giving real non-fabricated evidence that the definitions match the project's own convention, and my independently built conforming record (a deliberately different shape, with zero phase-reviewer entries) also passes, so the guard is not overfit to the worker's construction. Three findings, none blocking. The one that needs an orchestrator disposition is F-26.3-TQ-01 (MEDIUM): B1 replaced an ungated all-phases state-listing check with a phase-20-gated one, so docs/agent-contracts.md's '**all phases**' bullet is no longer what the script enforces - demonstrated concretely (a de-listed phase-15 reviewer report now PASSes where the pre-change script FAILed) - and the narrowing is disclosed in neither the worker report nor the limitations. There are currently zero violations at phase < 20, so nothing shipped is mis-passing today, but state.json is mutable and future de-listing of a historical reviewer report would go undetected. F-26.3-TQ-02 (MEDIUM, already disclosed by the worker) is the role_mix convention conflict with phase 20: it cannot let a wrong record pass, but it can reject a defensible record written by following the phase-20 precedent, and the contract never defines role_mix's basis. F-26.3-TQ-03 (LOW) is that the phase-reviewer portion of B2 is recomputed from the phase record's own subagents array, so an omitted phase-reviewer invocation is undetectable, which the contract's 'recomputed from the task-level records' wording overstates. Recommendation: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS, with F-26.3-TQ-01 dispositioned (either restore the all-phases check or amend the contract bullet and record the narrowing) and F-26.3-TQ-02 closed by stating the role_mix basis in the contract.
